## 2 data projects

- Johns Hopkins about child vaccination in the US
- EvalPsy: a tool for measuring psychological health at work, in France

## But... "typst in production"?

- in the data world, "production" can be confusing
- it means many different things
- here we're talking about:
  - generate 50+ parametrized pdfs and put them in a drive service
  - a web server
- very different use cases, but both generate pdf dynamically with typst

# Child vaccination in the US

## Project description

- Johns Hopkins University
- 51 reports (1 per US state)
- Reports are 4 pages long, with a bunch of charts, statistics, text, etc
- Open source + open data + public reports
- Project made with [claritydatastudio.com](https://claritydatastudio.com/)

## Tech stack

- **R**: all data work (fetch, clean and analyze data)
- **Typst**: pdf engine
- **Quarto**: interface between R and Typst that lets us "parametrize" reports

Quarto is developed by Posit, a company that financially supports Typst (https://posit.co/blog/posit-and-typst/).

## Parametrized reporting

- You define a template with fields that depend on a parameter (e.g., a US state)
- You dynamically generate the content (charts, statistics, logos, etc)
- You pass this content to the field
- You repeat this for each possible parameter (e.g., all US states)

In practice: we make a Typst template + Quarto handles the parametrized stuff. The only parameter here is the state name that we then use to fetch only specific data and generate all the content.

## Learn more about this project

- Right now project is finished: folks at Johns Hopkins are internally rendering the reports every once in a while with new data.
- Code + data + doc: [github.com/claritydatastudio/state-immunization-reports](https://github.com/claritydatastudio/state-immunization-reports)

# EvalPsy: measuring psychological health in France

## Project description

- Personal project with a friend of mine who's an expert in the topic
- Legal obligation in France for all businesses and public org to measure it every year, but:
  - no consequences if you don't do it
  - not clear how to do it
  - expensive if you hire consultants
- Goal: make this free, accessible, almost not time consuming and very simple

## How it works

- Someone from HR creates an account on our website
- get a link of a survey to share to all of his/her coworkers
- When everybody answered, he/she can generate a pdf with all results

## Tech stack (PoC, not stable)

- Backend: Python (fastapi for the API, matplotlib for dataviz, polars & sqlalchemy for data, ...)
- Frontend: native HTML/CSS/JS
- DB: Postgres

--> Future stack:

- React/Next for the frontend for simplicity
- Rust (framework TBD) for the backend because performance and memory usage can be issues here

## The PDF they get

- 50+ pages with dozens of charts, explanations and suggestions on what to do next

## Constraints

- Content must be entirely automatable and dynamic: charts, explanations, suggestions
- Run on a server
- Fully anonymous: we don't have any non-anynonymous data, but people may still be recognized in some charts small organizations. In this case, we replace the chart with a generic text placeholder.

## In practice

- Generate all content in Python
- Use https://github.com/messense/typst-py for direct Typst bindings
- Serve this to the client

# What Typst lets me do

## I'm not a software developer

- I _love_ to code, but...
- My clients do not care about my tech stack, they just want to "consume" data easily
- I don't want code to be a limiting factor of what I'm trying to do

## Typst makes me forget about how the report is made

- I create a Typst template with the design I want, and that's it!
  - it's fast
  - easy to code (and to maintain!)
  - bindings everywhere
- I can just focus on what matters to the clients/users
